01 · Executive summary

The interface now behaves like one product.

This review was run twice: once against a clean install on the review server, and once against the repository's seeded fixture for populated screens. The same code served both. The difference between a working install and a brand-new one is now explained rather than assumed.

The original review’s four release-blocking problems are gone. Mobile Watch holds every control on-screen, the guide scrolls as one surface, failed streams become a visible recovery state, and icon buttons are centred. The broader structural work also landed: one theme menu, one modal shell, one statistic component, one status badge, one type scale, responsive tables and a first-run checklist.

The evidence is not just visual. The post-change suite carries 58 end-to-end tests and 17 UX guardrails covering viewport overflow, off-screen controls, accessible names, heading/landmark structure, 12px minimum text, 44px primary touch targets, skeleton loading, theme persistence, dialog focus semantics and clean-install empty states.

7.7weighted score, up from 5.2
0horizontal overflow across audited desktop and mobile screens
0off-screen interactive controls in the clean mobile screens
0uncaught console errors in the populated walkthrough

The verdict

The product no longer needs a redesign. It needs the last operational cleanups — a shorter Settings surface, a shared playlist configuration boundary, a split Watch stylesheet, and automated accessibility measurement in CI.

05 · Remaining findings

What still needs work

Nothing here blocks a release. These are the items that keep the product at 7.7 rather than 8.5+.

P1

Playlist configuration still lives in Settings

IA

Sources now owns health and sync status, and Settings owns playlist/guide configuration. Cross-links make the relationship explicit, but adding a playlist and diagnosing it still means two pages. The original recommendation was to move the playlist editor into Sources; that was not done because it is a large stateful form and moving it would have duplicated or transplanted config logic.

NextExtract a shared PlaylistConfigComponent and render it from Sources, leaving Settings for automation, output and artwork. That completes the merge without duplicating state.
P1

Watch is still one 40.5 kB stylesheet

Engineering

The Watch component CSS remains over its 32 kB budget. Player, guide, recordings drawer, overlays, theme controls and responsive rules all live in one ~1,900-line file. That is why each polish pass keeps adding bytes instead of reducing them.

NextSplit into player, guide, recordings and overlay styles; move shared surface tokens to global. Target the 32 kB budget and a 20% reduction from the baseline.
P1

Accessibility is guarded by custom checks, not axe

Measurement

The Playwright suite now checks landmarks, labels, overflow, 12px minimum text, target sizes and date/theme persistence. It does not run axe-core or Lighthouse, and no screen-reader or five-user task test has been run. The 7.0 accessibility score reflects that gap; the interface itself passes the checks we do have.

NextAdd @axe-core/playwright with a zero-serious-violations gate, run Lighthouse on Dashboard and Watch, and run a five-user task test for add-source → sync → watch.
P2

Settings is still a long single page

Efficiency

Playlist, presets, guide duration, numbering, output and artwork are one scroll. The save button is far from the fields it commits, and on mobile the page becomes a long sequence of cards.

NextAdd a section rail and a sticky save bar that reflects dirty state; collapse presets behind a catalogue action.
P2

Mobile guide scroll has no affordance

Responsive

The timeline and rows now share one horizontal scroll, which fixed the clipping. On a phone the last category chip and later programme columns still sit off-screen with no fade, edge hint or “swipe” cue.

NextAdd an edge fade and a one-time “swipe for later” hint; keep the category row’s own scroll visible.
P2

Two type tokens now resolve to 12px

Tokens

Raising the minimum readable size made --font-2xs and --font-xs both 12px. The floor is right; the scale has a redundant step that will confuse the next component.

NextCollapse 2xs into xs or assign 2xs to a non-text role such as table-header tracking.
P2

Eleven themes is more than the interface needs

System

The picker now presents four curated themes with the rest behind “Show all”. Daylight and High Contrast are valuable; the remaining seven dark variants are mostly aesthetic and multiply the visual test surface.

NextKeep four to five supported themes, archive the rest, and test contrast and screenshots only for the supported set.

08 · Next

The last mile

The redesign programme is done. The next pass is narrower and measurable:

  1. Accessibility measurement: axe-core in CI, Lighthouse on Dashboard and Watch, then a screen-reader pass on the guide and player.
  2. Usability round: five users, three tasks — add a source, find why a channel has no guide, schedule a recording.
  3. Watch CSS split: player, guide, recordings, overlays; target the 32 kB budget.
  4. Playlist configuration extraction: one shared component, rendered from Sources.
  5. Settings section rail and sticky save.
  6. Mobile guide affordance: edge fade and swipe hint.

Bottom line

The product now looks and behaves like one system. The remaining work is about finishing the measurable edges — accessibility proof, task testing, and paying down one large stylesheet — not about another redesign.
